messages.content:
Extract limb-use facts from two consecutive actions. Return JSON only. Do not judge conflict. Use only explicit text; do not invent releases or extra grip capacity.
For PREVIOUS, report each occupied limb and the object/task occupying it at the end of the action.
For NEXT, report each limb required for the new action and the object/task that limb acts on.
If NEXT explicitly frees/releases/sets down/transfers/repositions the previous object before using that limb, list that limb in freed_before_use.
Use limb values LEFT_HAND, RIGHT_HAND, BOTH_HANDS, LEFT_FOOT, RIGHT_FOOT, BOTH_FEET, NONE.
Use short lowercase object/task labels copied or normalized from the text.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Amy keeps the tray in her left hand.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Amy extends her right hand to hand Amber a pancake.

Return {"previous":[{"limb":"...","task":"..."}],"next":[{"limb":"...","task":"..."}],"freed_before_use":["..."]}.

We need extract limb-use facts from two consecutive actions. PREVIOUS: "Amy keeps the tray in her left hand." So occupied limb LEFT_HAND, task? The object is "tray". Task maybe "keeps" but we use short lowercase labels copied or normalized from text. Likely "tray". For next action: "Amy extends her right hand to hand Amber a pancake." Limb RIGHT_HAND, task "hand"? Actually the action is handing a pancake. So task could be "pancake" or "hand"? The instruction says object/task labels short lowercase copied or normalized from text. In previous we used tray. For next maybe "pancake". But also "hand Amber a pancake" indicates hand as verb, but object is pancake. Use "pancake".

Also freed_before_use: If NEXT explicitly frees/releases/sets down/transfers/repositions the previous object before using that limb. It says extends her right hand to hand Amber a pancake. No mention of tray being released. So no freed.

Return JSON with arrays. Format exactly as specified.
